newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin wins opponent's praise for confronting Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Jospin wins opponent's praise for confronting Kohl.

text.p: France's Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin won unusual praise from a senior conservative opponent on Friday for standing up to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl over European integration.

Former interior minister Charles Pasqua, a senior member of the Gaullist party founded by President Jacques Chirac, faulted both Chirac and Gaullist ex-prime minister Alain Juppe for failing to confront Germany at times of tension.
Jospin "has proven that we don't have to accept the German position as sacrosanct," Pasqua told France Inter radio. "We don't have to accept what Kohl says as the law of the prophets."

"In the past there have been moments of tension in the Franco-German couple, notably between Jacques Chirac and Kohl, or even between Kohl and Juppe. But they never said it. They were wrong," he said.

France and Germany papered over a rift at a European Union summit in Amsterdam this week when EU leaders agreed to boost jobs and growth favoured by France, balancing a pact on budget stability championed by Germany.

The summit followed an open rift over the direction of economic and monetary union after Jospin came to power with an upset election win on June 1. He has said he will not impose extra austerity to qualify for a single currency from 1999.

Pasqua, 70, led the defeated "no" campaign to a single European currency before a 1992 referendum along with former National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin, who is expected to take over the leadership of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic Party from Juppe.
